description: §23.5.4 — inheritance covers a nested foreign construct. The OUTER `<program>` declares `capabilities=[network("api.example.com")]`; the INNER `<program name="probe">` declares NO `capabilities=`, so it INHERITS the closest ancestor's set (the outer's non-empty `network`). The `use foreign:probe` construct is therefore governed by a NON-empty set → W-FOREIGN-UNDECLARED-CAPABILITY does NOT fire. The positive complement to the no-union case: when the inner does not re-declare, it inherits the outer's declaration. CODE UPDATED S356 r4: the co-occurring Nominal refusal was `E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL` (fired at the `use foreign:` site); that code is RETIRED and the refusal now fires once at the nested-`<program>` DECLARATION as `E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL`. REGRESSION PIN: in S356 r3 BOTH codes fired on this file — and the second one's message asserted "there is no `use foreign:probe { … }` declaration in the parent" while line 3 of the case IS that declaration. It passed 894/894 because neither code was listed in `notCodes`. The retired code is now pinned absent here, so a resurrection of the twin cannot pass silently again.
rationale: §23.5.4: if a nested `<program>` does not declare `capabilities=`, the governing set is the CLOSEST ancestor that does — here the outer non-empty `network`. A foreign construct under a non-empty inherited set is declared, so the §23.5.5 presence-nudge stays silent. E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL co-occurs (the §4.12.5 sidecar runtime is Nominal, refused at its declaration per §4.12.3/§4.12.9). E-FOREIGN-010 does NOT fire: `probe` resolves — the `use foreign:probe` names the very `<program name="probe">` it sits inside, which is exactly the shape r3's subtree-excluding walk misread. COVERAGE NOTE: the harness contract is set-based (emitted ⊇ codes, emitted ∩ notCodes = ∅), so it cannot express "fires exactly once". The cardinality half of the invariant is pinned by `compiler/tests/integration/nested-program-sidecar-unclaimed.test.js`, which asserts by COUNT.
